expected: First feasible run. Accuracy 0.752-0.765 (point estimate ~0.758), time 9-14 s, against 59.3 s for the ResNet9 baseline. If accuracy is below 0.753, the next step is 11 epochs.
description: Build the first real recipe in submissions/arena/: an airbench96-style net without TTA. Settings: frozen patch-whitening conv (2x2, fit in prepare on real train images), dirac init, widths 128/384/576, depth 3 per block, BatchNorm-bias lr x64, Nesterov SGD lr 9 / wd 0.012 / bs 1024, label smoothing 0.3, lookahead, alternating flip plus translate-2 on GPU. The whole train set lives on the GPU as uint8 and is loaded in prepare. Use channels_last with bf16/fp16 autocast. torch.compile and warmup run in build() on synthetic data, covering the full batch, the final partial batch and eval shapes. Train for 10 epochs. Eval is a plain forward with no TTA and must handle any B from 1 to 1024.

expected: Accuracy drops ~0.6-1.0 pp from the 10-epoch run, to about 0.744-0.752 (infeasible). Time drops ~15%. Confirms that the missing TTA costs about 1 epoch.
description: Same recipe as the H1.1.1 base. Change only the epoch count: 8.5 instead of 10 (same schedule shape, scaled to the shorter run). This tests whether the published 8.5-epoch figure holds without TTA.
note: ideate: It duplicates I003, which already includes an epoch sweep that adapts to the I001 result (9, or 11 if 10 misses). Running a separate fixed 8.5-epoch point before the knee is known spends a run on a point that is probably infeasible. The H1.1.2 TTA-gap question can be answered from the fitted accuracy-vs-epochs curve from I001/I003. A point at about 8.5 epochs can be added later if that fit leaves it ambiguous.

expected: Accuracy rises roughly linearly at about 0.4-0.6 pp per epoch. 9 epochs gives about 0.753-0.756: feasible with ~10% less time than 10 epochs, or a near-miss that pins the knee at about 9.3.
description: Third point of the epoch sweep on the base recipe: 9 epochs, or 11 if the 10-epoch run missed 0.753. Fit accuracy against epochs with the 8.5 and 10 points and find the knee at 0.753 to within 0.5 epochs.

expected: Accuracy within 0.15 pp and time within 3% of the original run. This sets the inconclusive threshold for later comparisons and the safety margin needed above 0.753.
description: Rerun the feasible base recipe unchanged (identical commit config, fixed seeds 0-2) to measure the run-to-run noise floor from nondeterministic kernels and timing jitter.

expected: Accuracy drops ~0.3-0.5 pp and time is unchanged. Confirms LS 0.3 for CIFAR-100. If the drop is under 0.15 pp, mark it inconclusive.
description: Base recipe at its knee epoch count, with label smoothing 0.2 instead of 0.3. Nothing else changes.

expected: Accuracy drops ~0.3-0.6 pp (worth about 1 epoch) and per-seed spread widens. Time falls slightly (<2%) from skipping the averaging step. Confirms lookahead is worth keeping.
description: Base recipe at its knee epoch count with lookahead removed: plain Nesterov SGD, no weight averaging. Same lr, wd and schedule.

expected: At equal epochs, accuracy is +0.3 to +0.8 pp, so 1-1.5 fewer epochs are needed and time is ~10-15% lower at the knee. Risk: Newton-Schulz overhead and a large-batch accuracy drop could cancel the gain.
description: Explore: on the base recipe, switch the 4D conv filters to Muon (Newton-Schulz orthogonalized momentum, lr ~0.24, momentum 0.6, nesterov). Biases, BatchNorm and the head stay on Nesterov SGD. Use batch size 2000 with linear decay to zero, and keep the epoch count at the SGD knee.
note: ideate: It changes two things at once: the optimizer (Muon) and the batch size (1024 to 2000, with a new decay schedule). D002 recommends testing Muon first at bs 1024 against E002. It is replaced by a single-change Muon idea at bs 1024 and 9 epochs. Batch 2000 can follow if Muon shows a signal.

expected: Time falls ~8-12%. Accuracy drops 0.2-0.5 pp. Net gain only if adding back ≤0.5 epoch recovers 0.753.
description: Explore: on the feasible base, run the first ~35% of epochs on 24 px random crops and the rest at full 32 px. Compile both resolutions in build(). Same epoch count as the knee.

expected: Time drops about 5-10% against the base at the same epoch count, because Python and kernel-launch overhead is a noticeable share of a run near 10 s. Accuracy stays within 0.2 pp of the base, so feasibility is unchanged. If the gain is under 3%, the step was not launch-bound and H2.2 loses support.
description: Built on the first feasible airbench96-style base (I001/I003 knee). Make one systems change and leave the recipe alone. Move the whole training step into one torch.compile'd function: forward, backward, Nesterov SGD update and lookahead blend. Apply the update with torch._foreach_* ops (or SGD foreach/fused=True) so there is no per-parameter Python loop. Pass lr and the lookahead schedule as 0-d GPU tensors so changing them never triggers a recompile. Compile and warm up this function in build() on synthetic data, covering the full batch and the final partial batch. Keep the epoch count, seeds, lr, wd, LS and widths identical to the base.

expected: Accuracy about 0.7535-0.7540, extrapolating linearly at the measured 0.31 pp/epoch from 0.7552 at 9 epochs. Time about 7.9 s, down about 5% from 8.34 s. Feasible means a new best and refutes H1.1.2, which predicted 0.744-0.752. If accuracy is below 0.753, the knee is between 8.5 and 9 epochs and the next step is 8.75.
description: Change one thing in the E002 recipe: the epoch count, from 9 to 8.5. Scale the lr/lookahead schedule to the new total step count, so the shape stays the same over fewer steps. The last half-epoch uses the first half of that epoch's permutation. The final partial batch is still the shape that was compiled in build(). Everything else stays bit-identical to E002 (commit 479b9a3).

expected: Time down 0-8%, most likely about 3%, with accuracy identical within 0.05 pp. Under 2% means the conv algorithms were already near-optimal, and the remaining systems headroom comes only from the non-conv ops.
description: Target conv throughput: cuDNN conv kernels are about 75% of GPU time but run at only about 30% of bf16 peak. On the E002 recipe at 9 epochs, set torch.backends.cudnn.benchmark=True before warmup in build() and compile the model step with mode='max-autotune-no-cudagraphs', so Inductor benchmarks its Triton conv/GEMM templates against cuDNN for every shape (full batch, partial batch, eval) on synthetic inputs. All autotuning stays in untimed build(). If the base already has one of these settings, add only the missing one.

expected: Accuracy +0.2 to +0.8 pp at 9 epochs, worth 0.7-2.5 epochs of slack. NS overhead adds 3-6% per step. If accuracy is up by 0.4 pp or more and overhead is 6% or less, follow up at 8 epochs, where a net 8-15% time gain is expected. Accuracy within ±0.1 pp refutes H1.2.1 at this batch size.
description: Corrected version of I007 that changes only one thing. On the E002 recipe (bs 1024, 9 epochs, same schedule shape), optimize the 4D conv filters (all except the frozen whitening conv) with Muon: Nesterov momentum 0.6, lr about 0.24, 5 Newton-Schulz quintic steps in bf16, with the update scaled by sqrt(max(1, out/in)) on the flattened [out, in*k*k] matrix. BatchNorm biases and the head stay on the existing Nesterov SGD with the same lr/wd. Keep lookahead. Compile the NS loop in build(). Log the optimizer step time separately.

expected: Accuracy +0.3 to +0.7 pp at matched main-model steps. Proxy overhead +8-15% time. Net gain only if the accuracy gain is worth more than about 1.5 epochs. Most likely outcome: accuracy up, time up 10%, net neutral or worse at this horizon, which would weaken H1.4.
description: Explore the airbench96_faster-style batch selection idea. Each step, draw 2048 examples and score them with a tiny proxy CNN (whitening plus widths 32/64/64, depth 1, trained online on the same selected batches with its own SGD). The main model trains on the 1024 with the highest proxy loss. Keep the same number of main-model steps as the 9-epoch base (432), so the main model's per-step cost is unchanged and only proxy cost is added. Compile the proxy in build().
note: ideate: Proxy-based batch selection (H1.4.1, confidence 0.15) is expected to come out neutral or worse at ~9 epochs: it adds 8-15% proxy overhead for an uncertain gain. Muon (E014: +1.3 pp at 9 epochs) is a much cheaper source of sample efficiency, so this has the lowest expected value in the queue.

expected: Time -1% to -2.5% (8.05-8.18 s vs 8.257 s). Mean accuracy within ±0.15 pp of 0.7542; only tie-breaking in the max gradient can differ. If time improves by less than 0.8% (inside timing jitter), drop pooling as a lever. If the change helps, re-profile and take the next-largest non-conv kernel.
description: One systems change on the tip recipe (E007 commit 52204ad: 9 epochs, LS 0.2, cudnn.benchmark plus max-autotune-no-cudagraphs). Replace the final global adaptive_max_pool2d (and any other adaptive pool in the net) with an equivalent reduction, x.amax(dim=(2,3)), or F.max_pool2d with a fixed kernel equal to the spatial size. Its backward then becomes a dense masked/eq kernel that Inductor can fuse, instead of the atomic scatter kernel that took 0.48 ms/step (~2.5% of GPU time) in the E003 profile. The forward math is identical. Recompile and warm up in build() for the full batch, the partial batch and eval shapes. Nothing else changes.
note: E009 crashed: fix and relaunch, or drop it

expected: Time -4% to -6% (about 7.8-7.95 s). Accuracy -0.2 to -0.5 pp (0.749-0.752), probably infeasible given the 0.12 pp margin. A drop >=0.3 pp supports H1.5.1: the 576-wide block is worth more than its ~5% time, so the next move is a wider last block (640) with fewer epochs. A drop <=0.15 pp refutes it, and 512 becomes the new base, possibly with +0.25 epoch.
description: Test the width claim in the direction that saves time. On the tip recipe (E007, 9 epochs), shrink the last block from 576 to 512 channels and keep everything else, head input included, consistent. Block 3 is roughly a third of the network's FLOPs (conv1 at 8x8 plus two convs at 4x4), so this cuts about 5-6% of FLOPs. Record per-epoch time and per-seed accuracy.

expected: Accuracy +0.05 to +0.3 pp at the same time (8.26 s ±1%). A gain >=0.2 pp creates slack to retry 8.5 epochs (E006 missed by 0.2 pp). A loss means the airbench warmup suits CIFAR-100 already; then try the opposite direction (longer warmup) once before dropping schedule shape.
description: Schedule shape (D001 flagged that the tree has no node for it). On the tip recipe (E007, 9 epochs), change only the lr schedule's warmup: halve the warmup fraction (for example from ~23% of steps to ~12%), keep the same peak lr 9, and decay linearly to exactly zero at the final step. If the base already decays to zero, change only the warmup fraction. The lookahead schedule stays tied to step count as before.

expected: Time -4% to -7% (about 7.7-7.95 s). Accuracy -0.1 to -0.4 pp. If the drop is <=0.15 pp, this is a better trade than an epoch: one epoch costs ~0.9 s and ~0.5 pp near the knee. It would then combine with the warmup or Muon gains to stay feasible. A drop >=0.4 pp means early depth matters, so keep depth 3.
description: Explore where capacity sits. On the tip recipe (E007, 9 epochs), cut the first block's depth from 3 convs to 2: drop one 128->128 3x3 conv at 16x16 and leave blocks 2 and 3 at depth 3. This removes about 6% of the FLOPs, the cheapest-per-accuracy capacity if H1.5 is right that the late layers matter most for a 100-way head. Dirac init, widths and everything else stay unchanged.

expected: New best. Accuracy 0.756-0.764 (point ~0.760): E014's +1.3 pp at 9 epochs minus ~0.8-1.2 pp for one fewer epoch. Time 7.75-8.10 s (point ~7.95 s): tip per-epoch ~0.89 s plus ~0.09 s/epoch Muon overhead measured in E014, times 8 epochs. Below 0.753 would mean Muon's gain collapses at shorter horizons; then retry at 8.5 epochs.
description: Exploit E014. Port the E014 Muon optimizer exactly as it was onto the tip E010 commit (5aa9aa5: LS 0.2, cudnn.benchmark, max-autotune-no-cudagraphs, F.max_pool2d head). Muon settings: conv filters except the frozen whitening conv, Nesterov momentum 0.6, lr 0.24, 5 quintic NS steps in bf16, update scaled by sqrt(max(1,out/in)) on the flattened [out,in*k*k] matrix. BN biases and the head stay on the existing SGD, and lookahead is kept. Make ONE recipe change: epochs 9 -> 8, with the lr, Muon and lookahead schedules scaled to the new step count. The final partial batch shape is compiled in build(). Before launching, run the one-step finite-gradient check (drafts/debug_nan.py), because the compiled NS and Muon graph is new to the tip's compile mode. Log the optimizer step time separately.

expected: Time 3-5% lower than the 5-step Muon run at the same epoch count (~7.6-7.75 s if that run lands at ~7.95 s). Accuracy within +-0.25 pp of the 5-step run, which is re-draw noise. A drop >0.3 pp means the larger late-block matrices need the full 5 steps; then try 3 steps only on the 128-wide block-1 filters.
description: Cut Muon's per-step overhead. E014 added ~10% time, or ~1.9 ms/step, for NS. Take the Muon 8-epoch recipe above and change only the Newton-Schulz iteration count from 5 to 3 quintic steps, keeping the same coefficients (airbench94_muon uses 3; D002 C0013-C0015 show final quality is insensitive to exact orthogonalization). Keep everything else identical. Report the optimizer step time per step against the 5-step run.

expected: Accuracy 0.751-0.759 (point ~0.755). Time ~7.3-7.5 s, about 8-10% below the tip. If it is feasible, it reaches H1.2.1's <=7.3 s target region. If it is infeasible by <0.3 pp, combine it with the lr or averaging tuning below rather than trimming further.
description: Find the Muon knee below 8 epochs. Run this after the Muon 8-epoch run, and only if it scores >=0.758. Take the better of the 5-step and 3-step NS variants and change only the epoch count, from 8 to 7.5. Scale all schedules to the step count. The last half-epoch uses the first half of that epoch's permutation, as in E006.

expected: Accuracy moves by +-0.2-0.5 pp at unchanged time. A gain >=0.25 pp buys ~0.25-0.5 epoch of slack, worth ~3-5% time at the knee. Most likely the effect is within noise (lr 0.24 already near optimal); that settles the lr axis.
description: Tune Muon's lr, which was inherited untuned from CIFAR-10 airbench94_muon. On the Muon 8-epoch recipe (or 7.5 epochs if that becomes the tip), change only the Muon lr from 0.24 to 0.36. The SGD lr for BN biases and the head stays the same. If it falls by more than 0.25 pp, the follow-up direction is 0.16.

expected: Accuracy 0.5-1.2 pp lower than Muon with lookahead (most likely infeasible). Time ~0.5-1% lower, saving the lookahead blend of ~0.06 s. A drop <=0.25 pp would refute H1.2.2 and make lookahead removable, with averaging work moving to EMA.
description: Test whether Muon's update normalization replaces averaging. On the Muon 8-epoch recipe, remove lookahead (plain Muon + Nesterov SGD, no weight averaging) and change nothing else. Compare it paired against the Muon 8-epoch run with lookahead. This is purely informative about the H4.2/H1.2 interaction: it decides whether averaging tuning (H1.6) is still worth runs on the Muon base.

expected: Time -0.5% to -2.5%: the elementwise kernels are memory-bound, so the gain is mostly lost compute and smaller than H2.4.1's >=3%. Accuracy within +-0.25 pp. A time change under 1.5% is inconclusive by H4.1; if so, retire this lever.
description: Systems change that transfers to any recipe. On the current tip (the Muon successor if one is kept, else E010), replace GELU with SiLU everywhere and change nothing else. SiLU's sigmoid is cheaper than GELU's erf, and Inductor may fuse its BN+act backward with less recompute. Run the one-step finite-gradient check under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs first (E009 lesson), and re-profile the Triton elementwise share.

expected: Time ~8-9% below the Muon 8-epoch run (a 24 px epoch costs ~59% of a 32 px one, and NS cost per step is unchanged). Accuracy ~0.4-0.6 pp lower. It wins only if it beats the Muon epoch trade-off (~0.18 pp per 1% time); the likely outcome is roughly break-even, which would confirm low-res epochs as a worse trade than fewer epochs.
description: Combine near-misses. E013's progressive resizing saved 13.9% time but cost 0.8 pp, which was infeasible on the SGD tip with 0.2 pp of margin. Muon's extra accuracy may absorb that cost. On the Muon 8-epoch recipe, run only the first 2 epochs (25%) on 24 px random crops, with the rest at 32 px. Compile both resolutions in build(). Nothing else changes.
note: ideate: Its base (the Muon 8-epoch run) is no longer the tip: E018 runs 7.5 epochs. The trade is also known to lose. E013 measured low-res epochs at ~0.058 pp per 1% time, while cutting epochs on Muon costs ~0.13 pp per 1% (0.86 pp for ~6.7% time per epoch, E018). Spending accuracy on 24 px epochs is therefore about 2x worse than dropping whole epochs. Expected outcome: break-even at best.

expected: Accuracy 0.750-0.759, point estimate ~0.7555 (E018 0.7596 minus ~0.86 pp/epoch x 0.5). Time 6.80-7.05 s, point ~6.92 s (-6% vs 7.39 s). If feasible, this is a new best and gives a ~0.25 pp margin. Bank lr/tail gains before trying 6.5. If it is infeasible by less than 0.3 pp, keep the E018 tip and retry 7.0 after the lr 0.16 or the Muon lr floor change.
description: Find the Muon knee below 7.5 epochs. On the tip E018 (commit d634e3b: Muon NS3, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, lookahead, LS 0.2, 7.5 epochs), change only the epoch count from 7.5 to 7.0. Scale the lr, Muon and lookahead schedules to the new total step count. 7 epochs is a whole number, so the half-epoch permutation trick is not needed. The final partial batch shape stays the one compiled in build(). Nothing else changes.

expected: Muon step GPU time drops from 1.93 ms to ~0.6-1.1 ms. Total time falls 3-6%, from 7.39 s to ~7.0-7.2 s (point ~7.12 s). Accuracy within ±0.25 pp (re-draw only; the math is identical). A gain under 1.5% is inconclusive by H4.1 and means Muon overhead was FLOP-bound, not launch-bound. Applies to whichever epoch count is the tip.
description: Systems change to the Muon optimizer step only; the recipe math stays the same. Muon currently costs 1.93 ms/step of GPU time (about 10% of the step), mostly as many small kernels: 9 per-param calls, each with momentum, norm and projection ops plus per-iteration NS elementwise work. Replace them with one torch.compile'd Muon step over all conv filters. Do the momentum and Nesterov update with torch._foreach_* ops. Stack same-shape flattened filters within each block (128x1152, 384x3456, 576x5184 pairs) and run the 3 quintic NS iterations as one bmm per shape group. Apply the sqrt(max(1,out/in)) scaling and the weight-norm projection inside the same compiled function. Pass the Muon lr as a 0-d GPU tensor so schedule changes do not recompile. Compile and warm up in build() on synthetic tensors. Run the drafts/debug_nan.py one-step finite-gradient check under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs before launching (E009 lesson). Measure the Muon step GPU time with drafts/time_muon.py before and after.

expected: Accuracy -0.4 to +0.5 pp, point +0.15 pp: E019 shows the optimum is at or below 0.24, but it may be flat between 0.16 and 0.24. Time unchanged (±1.5% jitter). A gain of 0.25 pp or more is real and buys ~0.3 epoch (~4% time at the knee); then try 0.12. A drop of 0.25 pp or more puts the optimum near 0.24 and closes the lr axis.
description: Pre-registered follow-up to E019 (Muon lr 0.36 cost 1.04 pp on every seed). On the current tip (the 7.0-epoch Muon run if it is kept, else E018 at 7.5 epochs), change only the Muon lr for the conv filters from 0.24 to 0.16. The SGD lr for BN biases, whitening bias and head, the schedule shape, lookahead and NS3 all stay unchanged.

expected: Accuracy +0.0 to +0.4 pp, point +0.15 pp, at unchanged time (±1.5%). A gain of 0.2 pp or more supports H1.6.2 for the Muon group and stacks with the lr 0.16 result to allow ~0.25-0.5 fewer epochs. A drop of 0.15 pp or more (as with SGD's decay-to-zero in E012) means the floor helps; then leave the tail alone.
description: Lower the end-of-schedule floor for the Muon group only. E019's post-mortem says the Muon lr is an unbuffered per-step relative rotation, and the 0.07x terminal floor leaves end-of-training noise that lookahead cannot average out. On the current tip, change only the Muon group's lr multiplier so it decays linearly to 0 at the final step instead of to 0.07x. The warmup and the rest of the decay keep the same shape. The SGD group (BN biases, head) keeps its existing schedule, including its 0.07x floor. Lookahead is unchanged.

expected: Accuracy -0.4 to +0.4 pp, point +0.1 pp. Time unchanged. A gain of 0.25 pp or more opens a momentum axis (try 0.9). A loss of 0.25 pp or more suggests 0.6 or lower is right (try 0.45 only if the lr 0.16 result also points toward less aggressive updates).
description: Explore Muon momentum, inherited untuned from CIFAR-10 airbench94_muon at bs ~2000. On the current tip, change only the Muon Nesterov momentum from 0.6 to 0.8. Muon lr, NS3, lookahead and the SGD group stay the same. Rationale: at bs 1024 with a 100-way head, per-step gradients are noisier than in the bs-2000 CIFAR-10 setting. Heavier momentum averages more before orthogonalization, which normalizes away gradient magnitude, so momentum is the only knob that filters direction noise.

expected: Accuracy -0.5 to +0.6 pp, point +0.15 pp (C0017 reports a stronger early trajectory, which is what counts at 7-7.5 epochs, but this lr was tuned for flattened Muon). Time +0 to +3%: the NS FLOPs are similar, with 9 small bmm groups instead of one wide matrix. A gain of 0.4 pp or more is worth ~0.5 epoch and makes the frequency split the new Muon base. A loss of 0.3 pp or more closes the kernel-split branch.
description: Explore the D003 mechanism (C0016/C0017): how a 4D kernel is split before orthogonalization. Replace the flattened [out, in*9] orthogonalization with a real frequency-wise variant of Muon-C. Project each 3x3 kernel momentum onto an orthonormal real 3x3 basis (the tensor product of the 3-point orthonormal DCT-II), which gives 9 [out, in] matrices per layer. Orthogonalize them with one batched 3-step NS (bmm over the 9 frequencies), then transform back to the spatial domain. The output scaling uses sqrt(max(1,out/in)) on the [out,in] shape. Keep the weight-norm projection, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, lookahead and the epoch count of the current tip. Compile in build() and run the one-step finite-gradient check first.

expected: At 6.75 epochs: accuracy 0.750-0.759, point ~0.7548 (tip 0.7568 minus ~0.8 pp/epoch x 0.25). Time 6.25-6.50 s, point ~6.33 s (-3.5%). Feasible means a new best with ~0.2 pp margin. If it is infeasible by less than 0.2 pp, keep the tip and retry after banking an lr, tail or averaging gain. The run also pins the Muon epoch slope below 7 epochs: a slope above 1.2 pp/epoch means the curve is steepening and further epoch cuts need recipe gains first.
description: Trim the Muon knee by a quarter epoch. On the current tip (E023 commit 9c08ac0: Muon NS3 batched and compiled, lr 0.24, momentum 0.6, lookahead, LS 0.2, SiLU, 7.0 epochs; or the I027/I028 successor if either is kept), change only the epoch count from 7.0 to 6.75. Scale the lr, Muon and lookahead schedules to the new total step count. The last quarter-epoch uses the first quarter of that epoch's permutation, as in E006/E018. The final partial batch must be a shape compiled in build(); add it to the warmup if it is new. Nothing else changes. If I027 or I028 is kept with a gain of 0.2 pp or more, use 6.5 epochs instead (one epoch-count change from that tip).

expected: Accuracy +0.0 to +0.3 pp, point +0.1 pp (range 0.752-0.763 around tip 0.7568). Time unchanged within ±1.5%, since the blend has the same cost. A gain of 0.2 pp or more supports H1.6.1 and buys ~0.25 epoch; then try 0.98^5 or a sync every 3 steps. A drop of 0.2 pp or more means the window is already long enough at this horizon; then test denser syncing (every 3 steps, same per-step decay) instead.
description: Lengthen the lookahead averaging window on the Muon base. E020 shows averaging is worth ~0.9 pp with Muon, and the schedule (decay 0.95^5 x (t/T)^3, sync every 5 steps) was inherited untuned from CIFAR-10. On the current tip, change only the lookahead base decay from 0.95^5 (~0.774 per sync) to 0.97^5 (~0.859 per sync). That roughly doubles the effective averaging horizon late in training. The (t/T)^3 ramp, the sync interval of 5 steps, the final-weights handling and everything else stay unchanged.

expected: Accuracy +0.15 to +0.5 pp, point +0.3 pp. Time +3.5% to +6%, point +4.5% (~6.85 s at 7 epochs; block 3 is ~25% of step time per E011, and the NS cost grows a little). Not a new best by itself. A gain of 0.3 pp or more for 5% time or less beats the epoch rate, so follow up with 640 width at 6.5 epochs (net ~-2.5% time at equal accuracy). A gain under 0.15 pp means width returns have saturated at 576 under Muon; then close the width branch.
description: Combine the E011 near-miss with the epoch exchange rate. E011 priced block-3 width at ~0.13 pp per 1% of time, while cutting Muon epochs costs only ~0.056 pp per 1% (E022: 0.38 pp for 6.8%). So extra block-3 width paid for by fewer epochs should be a net win. On the current tip, widen only block 3 from 576 to 640 channels (a multiple of 64 for tensor-core tiling), keeping the head input and Muon groups consistent; the 640-wide filters stay batched as a same-shape pair in the compiled NS. Epochs stay at the tip's count. Run the one-step finite-gradient check under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs first, and warm up the new shapes in build().

expected: Accuracy -0.4 to +0.4 pp, point +0.1 pp. Time unchanged within ±1.5%. A gain of 0.25 pp or more means early steps are under-used at 7 epochs and buys ~0.3 epoch; then shorten the SGD-group warmup as a separate run. A loss of 0.25 pp or more (early instability with BN at full rotation size) closes the warmup axis for Muon. This is distinct from E012, which bundled a warmup cut with decay-to-zero for all params under SGD.
description: Muon's updates have a fixed magnitude (an orthogonalized step against a weight-norm projection), so the SGD-style warmup (23% of steps ramping from 0.2x) may waste early steps for the conv filters. On the current tip, change only the Muon group's lr multiplier during warmup: hold it at 1.0x from step 0, and keep the existing decay shape and floor after the warmup point. The SGD group (BN biases, whitening bias, head) keeps its full warmup schedule. Lookahead, NS3, momentum and epochs are unchanged. Check finite gradients for the first ~20 steps on synthetic data in drafts/ before launching.

expected: Time -1% to -4%, point -2% (~6.43 s): ~6.5% fewer FLOPs and memory traffic in block 1's first conv and its BN/SiLU, plus any gain from even-sized tiles. Accuracy within ±0.2 pp (re-draw only). A gain under 1.5% is inconclusive by H4.1 and closes conv-shape work. A gain of 3% or more supports H2.5.2.
description: Systems change to the conv shapes, with the learning recipe unchanged. First, in drafts/, print the activation spatial sizes per block and run a per-layer profile of the tip (untimed, not an experiment). If the unpadded 2x2 whitening conv outputs 31x31, block 1's first conv runs at 31x31, and max-pool(2) then floors that to 15x15, so its last row and column are computed and discarded. Make one change: slice the whitening output to [..., :30, :30] in the model's forward, identically in train and eval. This is a fixed architecture step, not TTA, and eval still accepts 32x32 inputs for any B. Every downstream pooled shape is unchanged (15/7/3); the only math change is that row and column 29 see zero padding instead of row and column 30. Warm up the new shapes in build() and run the finite-gradient check. If the profile shows the net already runs at even sizes (32/16/8/4), skip this idea and mark H2.5.2 not applicable.

expected: Accuracy +0.0 to +0.35 pp, point +0.12 pp (range 0.749-0.760 around tip 0.7546). Time unchanged within ±1.5% (~6.08 s). A gain of 0.2 pp or more supports H1.6.4 and banks enough margin to retry 6.25 epochs (~-3.5% time); then try 0.25x. A drop of 0.15 pp or more means 0.07x is near the optimum, which closes the Muon-tail axis.
description: On the current tip (E028 commit e95ff94: Muon NS3 batched and compiled, lr 0.16, momentum 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, LS 0.2, SiLU, 6.5 epochs), make one change: the Muon group's terminal lr floor goes from 0.07x to 0.15x. Shift the linear decay after warmup so it ends at 0.15x at the final step. Warmup shape, peak, the SGD group's schedule (floor stays 0.07x), lookahead, epochs and everything else stay unchanged. This is the untested direction opposite E025, where decay-to-0 cost 0.51 pp on the Muon group.

expected: Time -1.5% to -3.5%, point -2.3% (~5.94 s). That conv's dgrad is ~54 GFLOP of ~1.8 TFLOP per step (~3%), skipped on ~85% of steps. Accuracy within ±0.25 pp of 0.7546 (re-draw plus a tiny effect from freezing a 24-element bias). If accuracy falls below 0.753 by re-draw alone, keep the code and pair it with the next accuracy gain. A time gain under 1.5% is inconclusive by H4.1.
description: Systems change; the recipe is unchanged during the first epoch. On the tip, train the whitening-conv bias only for the first epoch (~49 of ~319 steps), as airbench94_muon/Hiverge do. After that, call a second compiled train-step variant where whiten.bias is detached / requires_grad=False. The whitening output then needs no grad, and the backward skips the input-gradient (dgrad) of block 1's first 24->128 conv at 31x31 plus the whitening-bias reduction. Compile and warm up BOTH variants in build() on synthetic data (full and partial batch) so the switch never recompiles in the timed region. Lookahead still blends the frozen bias (a no-op once it is fixed). Run drafts/debug_nan.py on both graphs under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs first.

expected: Accuracy +0.0 to +0.4 pp, point +0.15 pp (the averaged weights' activation statistics differ from the buffers accumulated along the fast trajectory). Time +0.8% to +2% (12 forwards at ~1/3 step cost ≈ 70-100 ms). A gain of 0.2 pp or more for 2% time or less supports H1.6.5 and allows 6.25 epochs at a net ~-2%. A gain under 0.1 pp refutes it: the buffers already match the averaged weights.
description: On the tip, after training ends and the final lookahead-averaged weights are in place (inside train(), so it is timed), recompute the BN running statistics. Reset running_mean/var, set BN momentum=None (cumulative average), and run a no-grad train-mode forward over 12 batches of 1024 training images: un-augmented, normalized as in training, bf16 autocast, channels_last. Restore the momentum afterwards. Compile and warm up this train-mode no-grad forward in build() on synthetic data. Before launching, check in drafts/ whether lookahead currently blends BN buffers; recalibration replaces them either way. The learning recipe is otherwise unchanged.

expected: Accuracy -0.3 to +0.4 pp, point +0.08 pp; time unchanged (±1.5%). A gain of 0.25 pp or more supports H1.7.2: short horizons want weaker regularization, which also raises the priority of H1.8.2 (drop translate). A drop of 0.2 pp or more closes the LS axis on the Muon base; then the 0.2-0.3 plateau seen on SGD holds here too.
description: On the tip at 6.5 epochs, change only the label smoothing, from 0.2 to 0.1. E004 tested LS only between 0.2 and 0.3, and only on SGD at 9 epochs. Hiverge uses 0.09 at ~7.65 epochs. Everything else (Muon, SGD group, lookahead, augmentation, epochs) stays identical.

expected: Time within ±1.5% of the tip (~6.0-6.15 s): E015 measured -7.5% from the conv cut, and +0.5 epoch adds ~7.7%. Accuracy -0.3 to +0.5 pp, point +0.17 pp (E015 measured -0.40 pp for the depth cut; +0.5 epoch is worth ~+0.57 pp). A gain of 0.2 pp or more supports H5.1.1/H5.1 and the depth-2 net becomes the base for further epoch trimming. Within ±0.2 pp supports H5's allocation indifference.
description: Test whether reallocating FLOPs from block-1 depth to epochs pays now that the Muon epoch slope is steep (1.14 pp/epoch for 7.5% time between 6.5 and 7). On the tip, cut block 1 from 3 convs to 2 (drop one 128->128 3x3 conv) and raise epochs from 6.5 to 7.0, with all schedules scaled to the new step count. These are the two halves of one time-matched reallocation. The Muon NS group for 128x1152 now has one matrix instead of a pair; warm up the new shapes, including the 7-epoch final partial batch, in build(), and run the finite-gradient check.

expected: Muon step from ~1.43 ms to 0.5-0.9 ms per step; mean time -1.5% to -4%, point -2.5% (~5.92 s). Accuracy identical to the tip up to re-draw (±0.2 pp). If the gate shows the 1.43 ms is mostly kernel time, not gaps, skip it and mark H2.4.4 refuted: the remaining Muon cost is FLOP- or bandwidth-bound.
description: Systems change, math unchanged. Gate it first in drafts/: compare the batched Muon step's wall span (cuda events around it) with the sum of its kernel times from the profiler. Launch only if the gap is 0.4 ms/step or more. If so, capture the compiled Muon step (foreach Nesterov momentum, NS3 bmm per shape group, sqrt(out/in) scaling, weight-norm projection) in a torch.cuda.CUDAGraph during build() on synthetic tensors. Use static .grad buffers (zero_grad(set_to_none=False)), a 0-d lr tensor updated with fill_, and parameters and momentum buffers that prepare() resets IN PLACE (copy_/zero_), so the captured addresses stay valid across trials. Replay the graph each step. Everything else stays unchanged.

expected: Time -3% to -6%, point -4.5% (~5.80 s): ~107 fewer Muon/lookahead steps (~0.15 s) plus larger GEMMs. Accuracy -0.7 to +0.2 pp, point -0.3 pp: one third fewer fixed-magnitude Muon rotations. That is likely infeasible at a 0.16 pp margin, but it tells us whether bs is a cheaper lever than epochs. If the drop is 0.15 pp or less, keep it, and the follow-up is Muon lr 0.20 at bs 1536. A drop above 0.5 pp refutes H1.2.3 and closes the batch-size axis.
description: On the tip, raise the batch size from 1024 to 1536 at 6.5 epochs (~212 steps instead of ~319), with all schedules scaled to the step count. The Muon lr stays at 0.16 (normalized updates). Scale the SGD group (BN biases, whitening bias, head) as batch size requires: if the code already uses airbench's per-example lr normalization (lr/bs), keep the configured values; otherwise scale the SGD lr x1.5 and keep lr*wd constant. Lookahead syncs every 5 steps as before. Warm up the new full and partial batch shapes in build().

expected: Accuracy -0.3 to +0.4 pp, point +0.1 pp; time +0.2% to +1% (one fused elementwise pass per epoch over 50k images). A gain of 0.2 pp or more for 1% time or less supports H1.8.1 and banks margin for 6.25 epochs. A drop of 0.2 pp or more means added difficulty hurts at 6.5 epochs, which raises the priority of H1.8.2 (removing translate).
description: On the tip, add per-image brightness and contrast jitter inside the compiled GPU augment, applied to the [0,1]-scaled images before normalization and whitening: x = (x - mean_img) * (1 + U(-1,1)*0.13) + mean_img + U(-1,1)*0.14, drawn independently per sample, with alternating flip and translate-2 kept. The RNG comes from the trial-seeded generator in prepare. Eval is unchanged. Warm up the new augment graph in build() on synthetic data.

expected: Accuracy -0.35 to +0.4 pp, point +0.05 pp (range 0.751-0.759 around tip 0.7546). Time unchanged within ±1.5% (~6.08 s). A gain of 0.25 pp or more supports H1.7.1: it buys ~0.25 epoch, so retry 6.25 epochs next, and also try head x0.25. A drop of 0.25 pp or more means the head wants a larger lr; then the follow-up is head lr x2 (one run). A result within ±0.25 pp leaves H1.7.1 open, and the next candidate is the BN-bias multiplier 64 -> 32.
description: On the tip (E028 commit e95ff94: Muon NS3 batched and compiled, lr 0.16, momentum 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, LS 0.2, SiLU, 6.5 epochs; or I037's successor if it is kept), make one change: halve the head (final linear layer) lr in the SGD group. If the code expresses the head lr as a multiple of the group's base lr, halve that multiple; otherwise halve the head param-group lr. Keep lr*wd constant for the head, which means doubling its wd so the decay per step is unchanged. BN-bias lr x64, the whitening-bias lr, Muon, lookahead, LS, augmentation and epochs all stay identical. Background: the head lr was inherited from CIFAR-10 SGD airbench (lr 9). That setting faced 10 outputs over ~10 epochs. Here the 100-way head trains against Muon-normalized features over 6.5 epochs, so the head may be overshooting. This is a pure hyperparameter change, so no new compiled shapes are needed. If the lr is passed as a 0-d tensor, nothing recompiles.

expected: Time -0.5% to -2%, point -1.0% (~6.02 s). Projection runs on ~15% of steps instead of all of them. Accuracy within ±0.25 pp of 0.7546 (re-draw, plus a small effect from filter norms drifting a few percent between projections). If the gate shows the projection costs under 0.15 ms/step, skip the run and mark H2.4.3 refuted: the projection is already fused into the compiled step. A run with a time gain under 1.5% is inconclusive by H4.1. Keep it only if accuracy stays >= 0.753; otherwise hold the code to pair with the next accuracy gain.
description: This is a systems change that alters the math only slightly. First gate it in drafts/ (untimed, not an experiment): use cuda events and the profiler to time the batched compiled Muon step on the tip with and without the weight-norm projection. Launch only if the projection costs 0.15 ms/step or more (about 0.8% of a ~19 ms step). If it does, make one change: apply the weight-norm projection only on steps where step % k == 0, with k = 2 + int(15 * step / total_steps), as Hiverge and Fable do. Always apply it on the final step so the end weights are normalized as before. Do this with two compiled variants of the Muon step, with and without projection, and pick between them in Python by step index. Never put a data-dependent branch inside the graph. Compile and warm up both variants in build() on synthetic tensors. Lookahead, lr and everything else stay unchanged. Run drafts/debug_nan.py on both variants under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs before launching.
note: ideate: Its point estimate is -1.0%, below the ~1.5% single-run timing jitter (H4.1), so a win could not be distinguished from noise or kept. The batched, compiled Muon step (E023) already fuses the projection, so it is probably far below the 0.15 ms gate. It also changes the math, which adds re-draw risk at a 0.21 pp margin. H2.4.3 stays open, to be bundled later with another systems change.

expected: Time -3% to -7%, point -5% (~5.6 s vs 5.894 s): 1.5 epochs at ~0.53 s plus 5.25 at ~0.89 s, against 6.5 at ~0.89 s. Accuracy -0.7 to +0.3 pp, point -0.15 pp (~0.7535), if a low-res early epoch is worth ~75% of a full one. Feasible means a new best. If it is infeasible by <=0.2 pp, keep the code path and retry at 7.0 total epochs (first 1.75 at 24 px). A drop >=0.5 pp means early full-res steps matter under Muon; then refute H2.3.2 and close resolution work.
description: Reallocate time from full-res epochs to cheap low-res epochs. The Muon epoch slope at the knee is now steep (~1.14 pp/epoch, ~0.15 pp per 1% time). E013 priced 24 px epochs at only ~0.058 pp per 1% on SGD, so low-res epochs should now be cheaper than full-res ones. On the tip (E034 commit f74c715: Muon NS3 batched, lr 0.16, mom 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, LS 0.2, SiLU, whitening bias trained only in epoch 1, ~6.5 epochs), make one curriculum change. Train the first 1.5 epochs on whole images bilinearly downsampled to 24 px (F.interpolate, antialias=True, inside the compiled GPU augment, after flip/translate). Then train 5.25 epochs at 32 px, for 6.75 epochs total. Scale the lr, Muon and lookahead schedules to the new total step count; bs stays 1024. The frozen whitening conv is reused unchanged. In drafts/, first print the per-block spatial sizes at 24 px input. Set the final pool for each resolution graph to F.max_pool2d with a static kernel equal to that graph's final map size. Do NOT use amax or flatten().max (the E009 Inductor bug). Compile and warm up every variant in build() on synthetic data: 24 px with whitening-bias grad, 24 px without it, 32 px without it, plus each full and partial batch shape. Eval stays the 32 px graph. Run drafts/debug_nan.py on every graph under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs before launching.

expected: Time -2% to -5%, point -3.5% (~5.69 s): ~63 fewer steps of Muon, SGD and lookahead overhead (~2 ms each) plus better GEMM efficiency at bs 2048 in the tail. Accuracy -0.5 to +0.15 pp, point -0.2 pp. The early, step-limited phase is untouched, so this should cost less than I042's fixed bs 1536. If the drop is <=0.15 pp, keep it (feasible at the 0.21 pp margin) and try switching at 50%. A drop >=0.35 pp means even the low-lr tail is step-limited here; then close the batch-size axis.
description: Batch-size ramp as a cheap form of lr decay (D008 C0091). Run this only after I042. Skip it if I042 (fixed bs 1536) holds accuracy within 0.15 pp, since fixed large batch then dominates. Run it if I042 drops more than 0.3 pp. On the tip, make one change: keep bs 1024 for the first 60% of training samples, then switch to bs 2048 for the last 40% (~127 tail steps become ~64). Total epochs are unchanged. All schedules (lr warmup and decay, Muon lr, lookahead decay ramp) become functions of the fraction of samples seen, not the step index, so per-step lr values at a given progress are unchanged. The Muon lr is unscaled, and the SGD group's per-step lr is unchanged; a larger batch at the same lr acts as a lower effective lr in the tail, where the lr is already decaying. Lookahead syncs every 5 steps as before. Compile and warm up the bs-2048 full and partial train-step shapes in build(). Run debug_nan.py on the new shape.
note: ideate: It was designed as a fallback in case fixed bs 1536 lost more than 0.3 pp. Fixed bs 1536 lost only ~0.18-0.26 pp and is now the tip (E041/E042). A ramp from 1024 to 2048 would be a step back from the current base. The bs-2048 question is now covered by a direct 1536 -> 2048 idea on the tip.

expected: Accuracy -0.35 to +0.4 pp, point +0.05 pp (range 0.751-0.759 around tip 0.7551). Time unchanged within ±1.5% (~5.89 s). A gain of 0.25 pp or more supports H1.7.1 and banks ~0.25 epoch (~3.5% time); retry 6.25 epochs next. A drop of 0.25 pp or more means the biases want a larger lr; the follow-up is x128 (one run). If the result is within ±0.25 pp and I044 is also neutral, the SGD group is flat and H1.7.1 is refuted.
description: On the tip (E034 commit f74c715: Muon NS3 batched and compiled, lr 0.16, momentum 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, LS 0.2, SiLU, whitening bias trained only in epoch 1, 6.5 epochs; or I041's successor if it is kept), make one change: lower the BatchNorm-bias lr multiplier in the SGD group from x64 to x32. Keep lr*wd constant for the BN biases by doubling their wd, so the per-step decay is unchanged. The head lr, whitening-bias lr, Muon, lookahead, LS, augmentation and epochs all stay identical. This does not depend on I044 (head lr x0.5); the two test different parts of the SGD group and can run in either order. Rationale: x64 was tuned for CIFAR-10 SGD airbench, where the conv filters moved at SGD rates. Under Muon with weight-norm projection, the filters rotate at a fixed relative rate, so BN biases at x64 may now dominate how fast the features shift. Pass the lr as a 0-d tensor so nothing recompiles; no new shapes are needed.
note: ideate: It was written for the E034 bs-1024 base. The SGD group has since been rescaled x1.5 for bs 1536 (E041), so the 'x64 vs x32' comparison no longer refers to the current per-step rates. H1.7.1's evidence (E039: head lr x0.5 costs 0.41 pp) points toward raising SGD-group rates, not lowering them. I053 (head x2) tests the more promising side first. Re-propose the BN-bias multiplier after I053 if the head axis turns out flat.

expected: Time -10% to -17%, point -13% (~5.13 s). The scoring forward costs ~1/3 of a step and the 512-sample step ~1/2, on ~85% of steps; the Muon/lookahead overhead is unchanged. Accuracy -1.6 to -0.3 pp, point -0.9 pp: the regime is step-limited, so steps are kept, but each gradient sees half the samples and BN batch stats come from a hard-skewed subset. That is probably infeasible on its own. At the knee an epoch is worth ~1.14 pp for ~15% time, so break-even is about -1.0 pp. A drop of 0.7 pp or less supports H1.4.1; then add epochs at the cheaper per-step cost (e.g. 7.0 epochs, ~5.5 s) to bank a net ~5-7% gain. A drop of 1.2 pp or more refutes H1.4.1 at this horizon and closes example selection.
description: Explore selective backprop without a proxy model (H1.4.1 has no test yet). On the tip, after the first epoch (the existing switch point where the whitening bias freezes), change each training step as follows. (1) Run a no-grad forward of the full 1024-image augmented batch through the compiled eval-mode graph, which uses the BN running stats and changes no state. (2) Compute the per-sample label-smoothed CE and take the top 512 indices with torch.topk. (3) Gather those 512 images and labels and run the normal compiled train step (forward, backward, Muon, SGD, lookahead) on them; the loss is the mean over the 512. The final partial batch of 848 selects 424. Epoch 1 stays at full batch, as now. The number of steps, the per-step lr schedules (Muon lr 0.16, SGD-group per-step lr) and the lookahead sync every 5 steps are unchanged, as are the epochs (6.5) and the sample stream. Compile and warm up in build() on synthetic data, using channels_last tensors of the exact layout used in the timed path (E035 lesson): the 512 and 424 train-step shapes (without whitening-bias grad), the eval-mode scoring forward at 1024 and 848, and topk/gather. Run drafts/debug_nan.py on the new train shapes under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs, and compare trial-0 and later-trial train times in the result to catch warmup gaps.
note: ideate: H1.4.1 has confidence 0.08 and its own point estimate (-0.9 pp for -13% time) is at break-even with the ~1.14 pp/epoch knee slope. On the E040 curriculum base it would need scoring and 512/424 train graphs for both the 24 px and 32 px stages, which multiplies the compile and warmup surface (E035-type leak risk) for a likely null-or-worse result. The 28 px stage and the boundary shift are cheaper ways to cut FLOPs per step, and E040 shows they work.

expected: Time +3% to +8%, point +5% (~6.19 s): ~105 more steps of Muon/SGD/lookahead overhead (~2 ms each, ~0.2 s) plus slightly worse GEMM efficiency. Accuracy -0.2 to +0.7 pp, point +0.25 pp, since 33% more fixed-magnitude Muon rotations help a step-starved run. At the epoch rate (~0.076 pp per 1% time), the change is a net win only if the gain is 0.45 pp or more. If so, keep it and cut to ~6.0 epochs (net ~-3%), which supports a small critical batch and refutes H1.2.3's direction. A gain under 0.2 pp means per-sample efficiency is flat between 768 and 1024, which raises I042's prior. A drop of 0.2 pp or more means 1024 is at or below the optimum.
description: Probe the batch-size axis in the direction opposite I042, so that both together pin the accuracy-vs-batch slope at a fixed epoch count. D009 C0110 says the optimal batch grows with horizon, so at ~320 steps it may be below 1024. On the tip, change only the batch size from 1024 to 768 at 6.5 epochs (~424 steps instead of ~319), with every schedule (lr warmup/decay, Muon lr, lookahead (t/T)^3 ramp) scaled to the new step count. The Muon lr stays 0.16 and momentum 0.8 (normalized updates). For the SGD group (BN biases, whitening bias, head): if the code uses airbench's per-example lr normalization, keep the configured values; otherwise scale the per-step lr x0.75 and keep lr*wd constant. Lookahead still syncs every 5 steps. The whitening bias trains for the first epoch, measured in samples (~65 steps). Compile and warm up the 768 full batch and the new final partial batch (50000 mod 768 = 80) for both train-step variants in build(), using channels_last tensors of the exact timed layout. Run debug_nan.py on the new shapes. This runs regardless of I042's outcome; its information value is independent.
note: ideate: The batch-size direction is settled by E041. 1536 cost ~0.2 pp for -8% time (~0.03-0.05 pp per 1%), much cheaper than cutting epochs. bs 768 would add ~10% time over the tip and could only pay off with a gain of more than ~0.8 pp, which flat-ish per-sample efficiency rules out. Its information value was conditional on I042, which has now been answered.

expected: Time -3% to -6%, point -4.5% (~5.46 s vs 5.718 s): 0.75 epoch moves from ~0.87 s to ~0.53 s per epoch. Accuracy -0.5 to +0.1 pp, point -0.15 pp (~0.7544). E040 implies a 24 px epoch is worth ~0.83 of a full-res epoch, with some fall-off once low-res runs past warmup. Feasible means a new best. If it misses 0.753 by <=0.2 pp, the follow-up is 2.25 + 4.75 (7.0 total). A drop >=0.4 pp means low-res steps are only cheap during warmup; then fix the boundary at ~1.5 epochs and try the 28 px stage (H2.3.3) instead.
description: Move the resolution boundary later on the E040 tip (commit 18ce8ac: Muon NS3 batched, lr 0.16, mom 0.8, lookahead 0.97^5, LS 0.2, SiLU, whitening bias trained only in epoch 1, 24 px bilinear antialiased whole images for 1.5 epochs then 32 px for 5.25, 6.75 epochs total). Make one change: train at 24 px for the first 2.25 epochs and at 32 px for the last 4.5, keeping 6.75 epochs total, bs 1024 and the same step-indexed lr, Muon and lookahead schedules, which do not change because the total step count is unchanged. If the switch now falls mid-epoch, take the first part of that epoch's permutation at 24 px and the rest at 32 px, so the sample stream is unchanged. The whitening-bias freeze stays at the end of epoch 1. Before launching, check that every shape used in the timed path is warmed up in build(): 24 px with and without whitening-bias grad, 32 px without it, and any new partial-batch shape at the switch. Warm up with channels_last tensors of the exact timed layout (E035 lesson). Run debug_nan.py on any new graph, and compare trial-0 and later-trial train times. Risk to note: E040's 1.5 low-res epochs covered roughly the warmup phase (~23% of steps). This change pushes low-res into the peak-lr phase, where full-res steps may matter more.

expected: Time -3.5% to -7%, point -5% (~5.43 s): a 28 px epoch costs ~0.77x a 32 px epoch, and 1.5 full-res epochs move to 28 px. Accuracy -0.5 to +0.15 pp, point -0.12 pp (~0.7547). 28 px keeps more detail than 24 px, so each epoch should be worth ~0.9 of a full-res epoch. Feasible means a new best and supports H2.3.3's claim that the 28 -> 32 stage carries most of the saving. If both this and the 24 px boundary idea are feasible, the next step combines them (24 px to ~2 epochs, 28 px stage, 32 px ~3.5). A drop >=0.4 pp means late-ish full-res epochs are not replaceable; then refute H2.3.3 and close the multi-stage line.
description: Add a middle 28 px stage to the E040 curriculum. On the E040 tip, make one change: 24 px for epochs 0-1.5 as now, then whole images bilinearly downsampled (antialias=True, inside the compiled GPU augment after flip/translate) to 28 px for 1.5 epochs, then 32 px for the last 3.75 epochs. Total stays 6.75 epochs, bs 1024, step-indexed schedules unchanged. In drafts/, print the per-block spatial sizes at 28 px input first (expect whitening 27 -> pools 13/6/3). Set the 28 px graph's final pool to F.max_pool2d with a static kernel equal to its final map size. Do NOT use amax or flatten().max (the E009 Inductor bug). Compile and warm up the 28 px train step without whitening-bias grad, plus any partial batch at the stage switches, in build() with channels_last tensors of the exact timed layout. Run debug_nan.py on the new graph, and compare trial-0 and later-trial train times to catch warmup gaps. Eval stays the 32 px graph.

expected: Accuracy -0.4 to +0.45 pp, point +0.12 pp (range 0.752-0.760 around tip 0.7559). Time unchanged within +-1.5% (~5.72 s). A gain >=0.2 pp supports H1.7.3 and banks ~0.2 epoch: next trim 0.25 epoch of 32 px training (~-3.8% time), and try head x3 as one run. A result within +-0.2 pp means the head lr sits at its optimum near 1x (E039 was the steep side); then close the head axis. A drop >=0.25 pp means 1x is the optimum from both sides.
description: On the E040 tip, double the head (final linear layer) lr in the SGD group. Keep lr*wd constant for the head by halving its wd. If the code expresses the head lr as a multiple of the group base lr, double that multiple; otherwise double the head param-group lr. The BN-bias lr x64, whitening-bias lr, Muon, lookahead, LS, the resolution curriculum and the epochs stay identical. This is a pure hyperparameter change: the lr is passed as a 0-d tensor, so there are no new shapes and nothing recompiles. Pre-registered follow-up to E039, where halving the head lr cost 0.41 pp on the then-tip.

expected: Accuracy -0.6 to +0.35 pp, point -0.05 pp. Time unchanged (+-1.5%; one extra scalar multiply). This is an explore idea. The smaller, less-whitened late updates act partly like a lower Muon lr, which is untested below 0.16. A gain >=0.2 pp supports H1.9.1 and banks margin for an epoch trim. A drop >=0.3 pp refutes it: full orthogonalization throughout is right at this horizon, and H1.9 closes. expected: If the gate passes: Muon GPU time -0.3 to -0.45 ms/step, mean time -1.2% to -2.0%, point -1.5% (~4.92 s). Accuracy within +-0.2 pp, point -0.03 pp: E017 showed NS5 -> NS3 cost nothing. A time gain >=1.2% with accuracy >=0.753 supports H2.4.5 and is kept. A drop >=0.25 pp means NS2 under-orthogonalizes the 128x1152 group; the follow-up is NS2 only on the 384/576 groups. If the gate fails, mark H2.4.5 refuted without a run: NS bmm is not where the remaining Muon time goes.
description: Cut one Newton-Schulz iteration using Turbo-Muon's AOL preconditioning (arxiv 2512.04632). Gate it first in drafts/, untimed: with drafts/time_muon.py on the tip's batched compiled Muon step, measure the GPU time of NS3 against NS2+AOL. Launch only if the saving is >=0.3 ms/step. At ~221 steps that is ~0.07 s, about 1.3%, which is near jitter, so a smaller saving cannot be graded. If the gate passes, make one change on the tip (E048 or its successor). Inside the batched compiled Muon step, after the existing pre-NS normalization, compute the first Gram matrix A = X^T X (or X X^T on the short side, as the existing NS uses). Rescale X by diag(rowsum|A|)^-1/2 on that side, rescale A to match so it is reused rather than recomputed, then run 2 quintic iterations instead of 3 with the same coefficients. The sqrt(max(1,out/in)) scaling, weight-norm projection, Muon lr 0.16, momentum 0.8, lookahead and everything else stay unchanged. In drafts/, also log the max singular value of the NS output for each shape group on a few real momentum matrices. Compare NS3 against NS2+AOL to confirm that orthogonalization quality matches. Run debug_nan.py under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs. Warm up in build() on synthetic tensors.
note: ideate: The gate is very likely to fail by the loop's own arithmetic. E016 measured an NS quintic iteration at ~25 GFLOP, about 0.15-0.2 ms of bf16 bmm. Removing one iteration therefore saves at most ~0.2 ms/step before AOL's extra Gram row-sum and rescale ops, which is below the 0.3 ms launch gate. Even if it passed, the point estimate (-1.5%) is inside single-run timing jitter (H4.1), so the run could not be graded. H2.4.5 stays open in case a profile later shows NS bmm is a larger share.

expected: Time -1.0% to -3.0%, point -1.8% (~4.91 s vs 5.000 s). That is ~24 fewer steps of fixed Muon/SGD/lookahead/launch cost (~2.5-3 ms each, as implied by E041), plus better GEMM occupancy on small low-res maps. Accuracy -0.30 to +0.15 pp, point -0.06 pp (~0.7546). Low-fidelity steps are ~free in the warmup phase (E040/E043/E047), and the Muon warmup axis is flat (E031). - Feasible and >=1.5% faster: keep, new best. Deprioritize I057. - Time gain <1.2%: per-step fixed cost is not where low-res time goes. Inconclusive by H4.1.
description: Raise the batch size only in the cheap low-res stages, as D016's 'cheaper variant' and C0235 suggest. The tip is E048, commit dc07126: bs 1536; 20 px bilinear antialiased whole images for epochs 0-1.5, 28 px for 1.5-3.0, then 32 px for the last 3.75; 6.75 epochs total; SGD-group lr x1.5; head lr x2 with wd halved; Muon lr 0.16, mom 0.8, NS3; lookahead 0.97^5; jitter; whitening bias trained in epoch 1 only. If I067 (16 px) or I069 is kept first, use that successor and leave its stage boundaries unchanged. Make one change: use bs 2048 for the first 3.0 epochs (150000 samples, the 20 px and 28 px stages) and keep bs 1536 for the 32 px stage. The stage boundaries in samples (75000, 150000) and the whitening-bias freeze at 50000 samples stay where they are. Index every schedule by samples seen, not by step index: the lr warmup/decay, the Muon lr multiplier and the lookahead (t/T)^3 ramp. The lr multiplier at a given progress fraction is then unchanged. Per-step lrs in the bs-2048 stages: - Muon lr stays 0.16 and momentum stays 0.8. C0218 says don't rescale at switches; C0210/C0212 say never raise momentum at a switch. - The SGD group's per-step lr is multiplied by 2048/1536 with wd unchanged, the noise-scale rule used in E041. expected: Time +2.5% to +4.5%, point +3.7% (~5.18 s). Accuracy -0.10 to +0.50 pp, point +0.25 pp (~0.7577). Exchange-rate grading: - Gain >=0.35 pp (>=~0.1 pp per 1%): low-res warmup epochs buy accuracy cheaper than any lever sells it (bs/curriculum cuts cost ~0.05 pp per 1%). That breaks H5's band. Keep the code and pair it immediately with the next time cut (I057 bs 2048 or I069). The pair should net ~-2 to -3% at equal accuracy. - Gain 0.15-0.35 pp: consistent with H5 (indifference). Discard. - Gain <=0.1 pp: the 20 px stage is saturated, or crossing the lr peak at 20 px costs what it adds (E043). Close stage-lengthening. Not a new best by itself.
description: Price the cheapest way to buy accuracy, a test H5 has never had on the curriculum base: extra warmup-phase epochs at 20 px. E040 says low-res epochs in the warmup phase are worth ~0.8 of a full-res epoch. At 20 px one costs only ~0.37 s, against ~0.82 s at 32 px with bs 1536. On the E048 tip (or its successor if I067/I069 is kept first), make one change: lengthen the 20 px stage from 1.5 to 2.0 epochs by adding 0.5 epoch, so the total goes from 6.75 to 7.25 epochs. The 28 px stage keeps its 1.5-epoch length (now epochs 2.0-3.5) and the 32 px stage keeps 3.75 epochs. Scale the lr, Muon and lookahead schedules to the new total step count, keeping the same shape. The whitening-bias freeze stays at the end of epoch 1, in samples. Where a switch falls mid-epoch, use the first part of that epoch's permutation at the old resolution and the rest at the new one. Add every new partial-batch shape at the 2.0- and 3.5-epoch switches and at the run end to the build() warmup, using channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). Run debug_nan.py on any new shape and compare trial-0 with later-trial times. Risk to note in the log: warmup now ends at ~1.67 epochs, so ~0.33 epoch of 20 px falls just past the lr peak, the E043 failure mode. This run is a pricing experiment. It is not expected to be keepable alone; it banks margin to pair with I057, I067 or I069.
note: H5 refuted

expected: Time -0.8% to -2.5%, point -1.5% (~4.85 s vs 4.928 s). Accuracy -0.40 to +0.15 pp, point -0.13 pp (~0.7533, borderline; E051's half-epoch cost -0.10 pp, and the price should rise as the 28 px stage reaches further into peak lr and decay). description: Lengthen the 28 px stage again and price the next half-epoch of the 32 px tail. The tip is E052 (commit 447a7db): bs 1536; 20 px bilinear antialiased whole images for epochs 0-1.5 and 28 px for 1.5-3.5, both without translate; 32 px with translate-2 for 3.5-6.75; jitter in every stage; SGD-group lr x1.5; head lr x2 with wd halved; Muon lr 0.16, mom 0.8, NS3; lookahead 0.97^5; whitening bias trained in epoch 1 only. Make one change: move the 28 -> 32 px switch from 3.5 to 4.0 epochs (sample 200000), so 28 px runs for 2.5 epochs and 32 px for the last 2.75. expected: Most likely no change to the metrics: all pairs differ, which refutes H1.6.6 and confirms that the flat lookahead/Muon-lr/head axes are really flat. description: Gate in drafts/, untimed. The submission changes only if a no-op is found. Check whether earlier hyperparameter edits actually reached the compiled timed path. (1) On the tip, log each lookahead sync's applied alpha and each step's Muon and head lr as read from the 0-d tensors inside the compiled graphs, and check them against the intended schedule. (2) For seed 0, train the E027 and E028 commits (lookahead 0.95^5 vs 0.97^5), E045 and E046 (Muon lr 0.16 vs 0.20), and E047 and E049 (head x2 vs x3). note: Gate answered from existing results, no run needed: identical commits rerun bit-identically in per-seed accuracy (E003), and every pair differs per seed: E027 vs E028 (lookahead 0.95^5 vs 0.97^5) [0.7544,0.7555,0.7539] vs [0.7556,0.7568,0.7515]; E045 vs E046 (Muon lr .16/.20) [0.7549,0.7560,0.7594] vs [0.7530,0.7590,0.7554]; E048 vs E049 (head x2/x3) [0.7527,0.7539,0.7589] vs [0.7558,0.7562,0.7525]. Code check: lookahead decay is a Python float applied eagerly, Muon lr is fill_'ed into a 0-d tensor argument every step, head lr is in the eager torch SGD. All edits took effect -> H1.6.6 refuted; the flat axes are really flat.

expected: Time -1.8% to -4%, point -2.7% (~4.80 s). Block 1 is ~20% of forward FLOPs, and the skipped backward work is ~20% of a 32 px step on ~20% of steps, plus the block-1 Muon group. Accuracy -0.6 to +0.1 pp, point -0.2 pp (~0.7526, likely infeasible alone): E037 showed block-1 capacity matters under Muon, and E025 showed tail diversity feeds the lookahead average. Feasible and >=1.5% faster: keep. Drop <=0.15 pp: keep the code and pair it with the next accuracy gain, or retry with the last 10%. Drop >=0.35 pp: refute H2.4.7; late block-1 updates matter.
description: FreezeOut-style late freeze of block 1. On the tip (E052, or I072's successor if kept), make one change. For the last 20% of training samples, from 5.4 epochs on, use a third 32 px train-step graph variant in which block 1's output is detached. Its conv filters and BN affine params get no gradient, but block 1 still runs in train mode, so BN running stats keep updating. Pair it with a second compiled Muon-step variant that excludes the 128x1152 block-1 shape group. The backward then skips block 1's wgrad and dgrad and block 2's first-conv dgrad. Pick the variant in Python by sample count, with no data-dependent branch in the graph. Lookahead still blends block 1 as now: the slow weights keep converging to the frozen fast weights. The SGD group skips block-1 BN biases (zero grad) through the same variant flag. In build(), warm up the new train variant and the new Muon variant, including every partial-batch shape at the 5.4-epoch switch, with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). Run debug_nan.py on the new graph and compare trial-0 with later-trial train times.

expected: Accuracy -0.5 to +0.5 pp, point +0.05 pp (structural explore; head lr x0.5 cost 0.41 pp, so the head is sensitive, but its lr axis is flat above x2). Time +0.1% to +0.8% (one small 100x576 NS group). A gain >=0.25 pp supports H1.10.1 and banks margin for the 28 px extension or I057. Within +-0.15 pp: the head's update geometry is not limiting; close H1.10. A drop >=0.3 pp means the SGD head's gradient-weighted directions are useful; refute.
description: Give the 100-way head an orthogonalized update. On the tip (E052, or I072's successor if kept), make one change: move the [100, 576] head weight out of the SGD group into Muon. Add it as its own shape group in the batched compiled Muon step: Nesterov momentum 0.8, NS3 with the same coefficients, sqrt(max(1,out/in)) = 1. Do NOT apply the weight-norm projection to the head, because row norms set the logit scale. Keep the head's current decoupled per-step decay (the same lr*wd product as now). Set its Muon lr so that the first-step update RMS matches the current SGD head's (x2) first-step update RMS, measured in drafts/ on real batch 0 of seed 0, and log that number. Use the same schedule multiplier as the Muon group. The head bias, if present, stays in SGD. In build(), warm up the new Muon graph on synthetic tensors and run debug_nan.py under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs.

expected: Time +0.4% to +1.5%, point +0.9% (~4.97 s; block-1 first-conv dgrad at 19-27 px for 2.5 more epochs). description: Test whether the early whitening-bias freeze limits the cheap curriculum. On the tip (E052, or I072's successor if kept), make one change: keep training the whitening-conv bias until the end of the 28 px stage (3.5 epochs, sample 175000) instead of until the end of epoch 1. This needs a 28 px train-step variant WITH whitening-bias grad, compiled and warmed up in build() (full batch and every partial shape at the 1.5- and 3.5-epoch switches), with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). The 32 px stage keeps the frozen-bias graph. Lr for the whitening bias follows its existing schedule. Run debug_nan.py on the new graph and compare trial-0 with later-trial train times.

expected: Time -1.5% to -3.5%, point -2.4% (~4.58 s vs 4.696 s): 0.675 more epochs at the block-1-frozen cost (~0.65 vs ~0.82 s/epoch at 32 px). Accuracy 0.7505-0.7555, point 0.7532 (-0.05 pp; this 10% lies at a higher lr than the last 20%, so it should cost a bit more per sample than E058 did). Feasible and >=1.5% faster: keep, new best; then price 0.6. Infeasible by <=0.1 pp: keep the code path and pair it with +0.25 epoch (the combine idea). Drop >=0.3 pp: the block-1 freeze is at its floor near 0.8; close earlier-freeze tuning.

The tip is E058 (commit fb3f626): bs 1536; 20 px for epochs 0-1.5 and 28 px for 1.5-3.5, both without translate; 32 px with translate-2 for 3.5-6.75; jitter in every stage; SGD-group lr x1.5; head lr x2 with wd halved; Muon lr 0.16, mom 0.8, NS3; lookahead 0.97^5; whitening bias trained in epoch 1 only; block 1 frozen from 5.4 epochs. If I077 or I078 is kept first, use that successor. Make one change: switch to the existing block-1-frozen graph pair 0.675 epoch earlier, at sample 236250 (4.725 epochs) instead of 270000. That pair is the 32 px train step with block 1's output detached, plus the Muon variant without the 128x1152 group, with block-1 BN biases skipped in the SGD group. Block 1 still runs forward in train mode, so its BN running stats keep updating, and lookahead keeps blending it. Total epochs, stage boundaries, bs, the sample stream and every schedule stay unchanged. The switch falls inside step ~153, so split that straddling step into the two partial shapes, as the existing switches do. Block 2 is the largest block, and late layers converge later than block 1 (C0237), so this should cost more per sample than E058. Likely infeasible alone at the 0.07 pp margin. Feasible and >=1.5% faster: keep, new best. Infeasible by <=0.15 pp with time down >=3%: keep the code path and pair it with +0.25 epoch. Drop >=0.35 pp: late block-2 learning matters; close the cascade at block 1 and refute H2.4.7's extension to block 2.
description: FreezeOut cascade: freeze block 2 for the last 10% of samples, following D025 (b) and C0239. Block 2 is frozen only after block 1, because in a skip-free net detaching block 2 cuts all gradient to block 1. On the tip (E058, or the successor of the block-1-at-0.7 idea, I077 or I078 if one is kept), make one change: from sample 303750 (6.075 epochs, 0.9 of samples) to the end, use a fourth 32 px train-step graph variant in which block 2's output is detached. Blocks 1 and 2 still run forward in train mode, so their BN running stats keep updating. Pair it with a third compiled Muon-step variant that contains only the 576-wide block-3 shape group, and skip block-1 and block-2 BN biases in the SGD group through the same variant flag. The backward then skips block 2's wgrad and dgrad and block 3's first-conv dgrad. Conv FLOPs per step fall from ~0.81x to ~0.49x of an unfrozen 32 px step. Lookahead still blends blocks 1 and 2. Pick the variant in Python by sample count, with no data-dependent branch in the graph. Split the straddling step at 303750 into the two partial shapes. In build(), warm up the new train and Muon variants plus every partial shape at the 0.9 switch and at the run end, with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). Keep build under ~450 s. Run debug_nan.py on the new graph and compare trial-0 with later-trial train times.

expected: If both freeze cuts are stacked (block 1 from 0.7, block 2 from 0.9): 32 px time ~2.32 s against the tip's ~2.44 s, so total time ~4.58 s (-2.4%, range -1% to -4%). Accuracy 0.751-0.758, point 0.7545: the stack costs ~-0.2 pp and +0.25 epoch adds ~+0.25-0.3 pp. Feasible and >=1% faster than the then-tip: keep, new best with ~0.15 pp margin, and continue the freeze-more-plus-epochs ladder (block 1 at 0.6). If it is feasible but not faster, the freeze cost per sample is rising faster than estimated; stop the ladder.
description: Cash in the freeze exchange rate as margin. Freezing costs ~0.02-0.05 pp per 1% of time, while 32 px epochs buy ~0.08-0.15 pp per 1%, so freeze-more plus more epochs should net time at equal accuracy. Run this only after the block-1-at-0.7 and block-2-cascade ideas have been read. Base: the faster feasible commit among them if one was kept. Otherwise stack every freeze change that was infeasible by <=0.15 pp onto E058; if neither qualifies, skip this idea. Make one change: total epochs 6.75 -> 7.0, with the extra 0.25 epoch added to the 32 px stage (stage boundaries at 1.5 and 3.5 epochs stay in samples). Scale the lr warmup and decay, the Muon multiplier and the lookahead (t/T)^3 ramp to samples seen. Keep the freeze points as fractions of total samples (for example 0.7 and 0.9), so they move proportionally. The last quarter-epoch uses the first quarter of that epoch's permutation, as in E027. In build(), warm up every new partial shape at the moved freeze switches and at the new run end for each graph variant, with channels_last tensors in the exact timed layout (E035). Run debug_nan.py on new shapes and compare trial-0 with later-trial times.

expected: Time -2.5% to -4.5%, point -3.4% (~4.54 s): about half of 1.9 epochs moves to the frozen cost (~0.17 s/epoch saved on half the steps). Accuracy 0.749-0.755, point 0.7525 (-0.12 pp). Grading against the block-1-at-0.7 idea, which saves ~2.4%: if thinning costs less accuracy per 1% of time than the hard earlier freeze, block 1 needs recency of updates rather than update count; then stack thinning over 0.3-0.8 with the 0.8 freeze. A drop >=0.3 pp means block-1 updates at peak or mid lr carry real value per step; then only tail freezing is cheap. Feasible and >=1.5% faster: keep.
description: Partial freezing by update thinning, as an explore against a hard earlier freeze. On the tip (E058 or its successor), make one change: during the 32 px stage before the existing freeze (samples 175000-270000, epochs 3.5-5.4), run the existing block-1-frozen graph pair (detached block-1 output, and the Muon variant without the 128x1152 group) on every odd step, and the normal graph pair on even steps. On frozen steps block 1 gets no gradient: its Muon momentum buffer is not updated and its BN biases are skipped in SGD, while its BN running stats still update. The lr schedules are unchanged, so block 1 takes half as many rotations in that window, each from a full-batch gradient. Pick the variant in Python by step parity, with no data-dependent branch. No new graphs are needed, since both variants already exist at 32 px. Warm up any new partial shape at the 3.5-epoch and 5.4-epoch switches with both variants in the exact timed layout (E035). Compare trial-0 with later-trial times.

expected: Accuracy -0.35 to +0.30 pp, point 0.0 pp (~0.7537). Time +0% to +0.5% (one extra norm and scale per group). A gain >=0.2 pp supports H1.9: late, less-whitened updates help at fixed magnitude, which banks margin for the freeze ladder. Within +-0.15 pp: orthogonalization strength is not a lever at this horizon; close H1.9 and drop H1.9.1. A drop >=0.3 pp means full whitening throughout is right, consistent with E030's lesson that equalizing directions the gradient barely asked for can hurt.
description: RMS-matched test of scheduled orthogonalization strength. This is the form requested when I054 was dropped, so that a result is not confounded with a lower effective Muon lr (H1.2.4). On the tip (E058 or its successor), make one change inside the batched compiled Muon step. Today each momentum matrix is scaled to Frobenius norm 1 before NS3. Instead, scale it to s_t, which decays linearly from 0.50 at step 0 to 0.08 at the final step (Hiverge's CIFAR-10 schedule). Run the same 3 quintic iterations, then rescale each NS output matrix so its Frobenius norm equals that of the tip's NS output for that shape group (or, more simply, sqrt(min(out,in)) times the existing sqrt(max(1,out/in)) factor). The per-step update magnitude is therefore unchanged, and only how strongly the small singular directions are flattened changes. Pass s_t as a 0-d GPU tensor updated with fill_, so nothing recompiles. Weight-norm projection, Muon lr 0.16, momentum 0.8, lookahead, the curriculum, freeze points and epochs stay unchanged. In drafts/, log the per-group update Frobenius norm and the fraction of singular values above 0.5 at steps 0, 100 and the end, against the tip, to confirm the norms match and the spectrum is less whitened late in training. Run debug_nan.py under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs and re-warm the Muon variants in build().

expected: Accuracy -0.30 to +0.35 pp, point +0.05 pp. Paired with per-filter weight-norm projection, equal per-filter update RMS gives every filter a more even relative rotation. NorMuon is untested on CNN filters. Time +0.2% to +1.0%, point +0.5% (one memory-bound pass over ~11M params per step). A gain >=0.25 pp supports H1.2.6 and banks margin for the freeze ladder. Within +-0.15 pp: Muon's update geometry is saturated on the filters; close H1.2.6. A drop >=0.25 pp refutes it.
description: NorMuon on the conv filters. On the tip (E058 or its successor), make one change inside the batched compiled Muon step: after NS3 and before the sqrt(max(1,out/in)) scaling, apply per-row (per output filter) second-moment normalization. Keep a buffer v per group of shape [n_mats, out, 1], initialised to zero in prepare() (reset per trial). Update v = 0.95*v + 0.05*mean_over_cols(O^2) and set O' = O / sqrt(v_hat + 1e-8), with bias correction v_hat = v / (1 - 0.95^t). Then rescale O' to the Frobenius norm O had, so the per-step update magnitude is unchanged and only its distribution across filters changes. The weight-norm projection, Muon lr 0.16, momentum 0.8, lookahead, curriculum, freeze variants and epochs stay unchanged. The frozen-block Muon variants must update v only for the groups they contain. Pass the step count as a 0-d tensor. Re-warm all Muon variants in build() on synthetic tensors, and run debug_nan.py under max-autotune-no-cudagraphs.
